files.lesson.md: --- order: 41 unit: composite10 node: AC9M10M01 n2 uses: [AC9M10M01 n1, AC9M9M01 n1, AC9M8M06 n1] assumes: [AC9M10M01 n1] connection: grain-silo title: Surface area of composite objects summary: "Count only the faces you can see: faces that are joined together are hidden, and a hole adds an inside surface. Paint on a silo, a stack of boxes and a pipe." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A farm silo needs a fresh coat of paint. How much paint does it need?" --- The silo is the one from last lesson: a cylinder wall 6 m tall with a radius of 2 m, and a cone roof 1.5 m tall. The roof slopes, and its sloping side is 2.5 m long. You paint the wall and the roof, but not the ground the silo stands on (sizes made up for the task). How many square metres need paint? Have a guess, and we'll come back to it at the end. ## Predict: paint for the silo ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to the painted area shows who counts the joined circles or the ground circle, and who forgets the roof." check: type: predict q: "The silo has a cylinder wall (6 m tall, radius 2 m) and a cone roof with a slant length of 2.5 m. About how many square metres need paint?" options: - "About 91 m²" - "About 116 m²" - "About 104 m²" - "About 75 m²" actual: "About 91 m². The wall is about 75 m² and the roof about 16 m². The flat circles aren't painted: the cone's base and the cylinder's top are joined, and the cylinder's base is on the ground." ``` The picture isn't to scale. Which of the silo's surfaces could a painter reach? ## Run: the roof ```step stage: run insight: "The curved face of a cone has area π × r × l, where l is the slant length along the sloping side. It is the slant length, not the height up the middle." check: { type: number, q: "The roof cone has a radius of $2$ m and a slant length of $2.5$ m. What is the area of its curved face? (m², 1 decimal place, $\\pi \\approx 3.14$)", answer: 15.7, tolerance: 0.1, explain: "3.14 × 2 × 2.5 = 15.7 m²." } ``` Here is a fact to use rather than one we prove today: the curved face of a cone has an area of $\pi r l$, where $r$ is the radius and $l$ is the **slant length**, the distance along the sloping side from the point to the edge. It is not the height up the middle, $h$. A cylinder's curved wall is $2 \pi r h$. The wall is $2 \times 3.14 \times 2 \times 6$. How big is it next to the roof? ## Investigate: only what you can see ```step stage: investigate insight: "The surface area of a composite object is the faces on the outside only. Faces that are joined are hidden, and a hole adds an inside surface. Mei counts the joined circles." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Which of the silo's surfaces are painted?" options: - "The cylinder's curved wall and the cone's curved roof" - "The wall, the roof and the circle where the cone meets the cylinder" - "The wall, the roof and the cylinder's circular base on the ground" - "All five faces: the wall, the roof and the three circles" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "The join is hidden inside. Neither circle that makes it is on the outside." - "The base sits on the ground. Nobody can paint it." - "Three of those faces are flat circles, and none of them can be seen." explain: "Only the curved wall and the curved roof are on the outside. All three flat circles are hidden: two are pressed together and one is on the ground." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "How many flat circles do the cylinder and the cone have between them?", answer: 3, explain: "The cylinder's top and base, and the cone's base." } - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mei" text: "Mei works out the paint for the silo. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: join-faces-counted explain: "Line 4: the two circles at the join are pressed together, so they are inside the silo and aren't painted. Mei added them, 25.1 m², too much." - check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The concrete pipe from last lesson is 2 m long, with an outer radius of 0.5 m and a hole radius of 0.4 m (made up for the task). It is open at both ends. A painter coats every surface: the outside, the inside and the two ring-shaped ends. What is the total area? (m², 1 decimal place, $\\pi \\approx 3.14$)" steps: - ["$A_{\\text{outside}} = 2 \\times 3.14 \\times 0.5 \\times 2 = 6.28$", "the outer curved surface"] - ["$A_{\\text{inside}} = 2 \\times 3.14 \\times 0.4 \\times 2 = 5.024$", "the hole adds an inside surface"] - ["$A_{\\text{ends}} = 2 \\times (3.14 \\times 0.5^2 - 3.14 \\times 0.4^2) = 0.5652$", "two rings: the big circle minus the hole"] - ["$A = 6.28 + 5.024 + 0.5652 = 11.87$", "add all four surfaces"] answer: "11.9" answerLabel: "Painted area (m²)" tolerance: 0.1 feedback: - ["11.3", "The two ring-shaped ends are surfaces too: add them."] - ["6.8", "A hole has an inside wall. Add the inside surface as well."] criteria: - "I counted the outside, the inside and both ends." - "I found each ring end as a big circle minus the hole." - "I used the radius, not the diameter." explain: "6.28 + 5.024 + 0.5652 = 11.8692, about 11.9 m²." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "The pipe is open at both ends. How many separate surfaces does it have: the outside, the inside and how many ends?", answer: 4, explain: "Outside, inside and two ends: four surfaces." } ``` ### Only what you can see A small seed silo (made up): a cylinder wall 5 m tall with a radius of 1.5 m, and a cone roof 2 m tall. Its slant length isn't given, so you have to find it first. Pythagoras works on the right-angled triangle inside the cone. ```worked l = \sqrt{1.5^2 + 2^2} = 2.5 :: The slant length is the long side of the triangle with legs r and h. A_{\text{wall}} = 2 \times 3.14 \times 1.5 \times 5 = 47.1 :: Curved wall, 2πrh, in m². A_{\text{roof}} = 3.14 \times 1.5 \times 2.5 = 11.775 :: Curved roof, πrl. A = 47.1 + 11.775 = 58.875 \approx 58.9 \text{ m}^2 :: Add the two outside faces. No circles: they are hidden. ``` Now look at the big silo and decide which faces are on the outside. ### Find the mistake Read Mei's working. Which line counts faces that nobody can see? ### A pipe, inside and out Work out the area of every surface on paper first, one step per line, then type the total. ## Modify: change one thing ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a steeper roof needs a new slant length, a taller wall changes only the cylinder, and two glued cubes lose the faces that touch." tasks: - hint: ["It's the long side of a right-angled triangle.", "3² + 4² = 25."] check: { type: number, q: "A roof cone has a radius of $3$ m and a height of $4$ m. What is its slant length? (m)", answer: 5, explain: "l = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 m." } - hint: ["Only the wall changes.", "The roof is still 15.7 m²."] check: { type: number, q: "The silo's wall is raised to $8$ m (radius $2$ m, same roof with slant length $2.5$ m). How many square metres need paint? (1 decimal place, $\\pi \\approx 3.14$)", answer: 116.2, tolerance: 0.2, explain: "Wall 2 × 3.14 × 2 × 8 = 100.48, roof 15.7. Total 116.18 m²." } - hint: ["One cube has 6 faces of 4 m².", "Two faces disappear in the glue."] check: { type: number, q: "Edge case: two cubes, each with sides of $2$ m, are glued face to face to make a long box $2$ m by $2$ m by $4$ m. What is the surface area of the long box? (m²)", answer: 40, feedback: [["48", "That counts the two faces that are glued together."]], explain: "Each cube is 6 × 4 = 24 m², so 48 together. The glue hides two 4 m² faces: 48 − 8 = 40 m². The long box is 2 × (4 + 8 + 8) = 40 m²." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is the surface area of one cube with sides of $2$ m? (m²)", answer: 24, explain: "6 faces of 2 × 2 = 4 m²." } ``` ### A steeper roof ### A taller wall ### Two cubes ## Practise: composite surface areas ```step stage: practise insight: "Counting only the outside faces: a stack, a drilled cube, and the review of the volume with the same hole." tasks: - hint: ["Add the surface areas of the two boxes, then take away what is hidden.", "The hidden part is the touching face, counted twice."] check: type: number q: "A box $4$ m by $3$ m by $2$ m has a smaller box, $2$ m by $3$ m by $1$ m, standing on its top. The small box's $2$ by $3$ face sits flat on the top, wholly on it. What is the surface area of the whole stack, including the bottom? (m²)" answer: 62 feedback: - ["74", "That adds the two boxes' full surface areas, and the touching faces are hidden."] explain: "The big box is 2 × (12 + 8 + 6) = 52. The small box is 2 × (6 + 2 + 3) = 22. The touching face is 6 m², hidden on both: 52 + 22 − 12 = 62 m²." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is the area of the face where the two boxes touch? (m²)", answer: 6, explain: "The small box's 2 by 3 face: 6 m²." } - hint: ["The cube has 6 faces of 4 × 4.", "The hole removes two 1 × 1 squares and adds four walls of 4 × 1."] check: type: number q: "A cube with sides of $4$ cm has a square hole $1$ cm by $1$ cm drilled straight through the middle, from one face to the opposite one. What is its surface area? (cm²)" answer: 110 feedback: - ["94", "The hole takes away two squares, but it also adds walls inside. Count the four inside walls."] explain: "A plain cube is 6 × 16 = 96. The hole removes two 1 cm² squares: 94. It adds four inside walls of 4 × 1 = 4 cm² each, which is 16: 110 cm²." - check: type: number q: "Review: the cube with the hole through it. What is its volume? (cm³)" answer: 60 explain: "The cube is 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cm³. The hole is 1 × 1 × 4 = 4 cm³. Taking it away leaves 60 cm³." ``` ### The stack ### A hole ### Review ## Make: paint for the silo ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the silo: find only the outside faces, and turn the area into litres of paint." tasks: - hint: ["Which faces are painted?", "The slant length is given in the picture: 2.5 m."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The silo has a cylinder wall 6 m tall with a radius of 2 m, and a cone roof with a slant length of 2.5 m (made up for the task). What area needs paint? (m², 1 decimal place, $\\pi \\approx 3.14$)" steps: - ["Painted: the curved wall and the curved roof. The circles are hidden.", "choose the faces first"] - ["$A_{\\text{wall}} = 2 \\times 3.14 \\times 2 \\times 6 = 75.36$", "the wall"] - ["$A_{\\text{roof}} = 3.14 \\times 2 \\times 2.5 = 15.7$", "the roof"] - ["$A = 75.36 + 15.7 = 91.06$", "add the two painted faces"] answer: "91.1" answerLabel: "Painted area (m²)" tolerance: 0.2 feedback: - ["116.2", "That counts both circles at the join. They are hidden."] - ["103.6", "That counts the circle on the ground. Nobody paints it."] - ["75.4", "That is the wall only. The roof needs paint too."] criteria: - "I decided which faces are painted before calculating." - "I did not count the circles." - "I used πrl for the roof." explain: "75.36 + 15.7 = 91.06, so about 91.1 m²." - hint: ["Divide the painted area by what one litre covers.", "Rounding up: a little unpainted is worse than a little spare."] check: type: number q: "A litre of paint covers $10$ m² (made up for the task). How many whole litres do you need for one coat on the silo, rounding up?" answer: 10 feedback: - ["9", "9 litres covers only 90 m², and the silo is a little over 91. Round up."] explain: "91.06 ÷ 10 = 9.1 litres. Rounded up to a whole litre, that is 10." ``` ### The silo, on paper Back to the silo. Work it out on paper first, then type your answer. ### Litres of paint **Also used in** - **Painting and cladding.** Any job that covers a surface needs the area of the outside faces only. - **Packaging.** A box stacked on a box, or a tube with a hole, is a composite solid. - **Next lesson.** Volume of composite objects: how much the silo and a tank hold, and what a model leaves out. ```teacher summary: "Students find the surface area of a composite object by counting only the faces on the outside: joined faces are hidden and a hole adds an inside surface (AC9M10M01, node 2)." time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can say which faces of a composite object are on the outside. - I can leave out the faces that are joined. - I can add the inside surface of a hole. struggle: "Adding every face of every solid. Ask: can a painter reach this face?" before: > Students need Break it into solids and Surface area from nets (Year 9). This is a hinge lesson: the folded easier questions let students count the flat circles first. The one idea: the surface area is the outside faces only. Joined faces are hidden (counted for neither solid), and a hole adds an inside surface. The curved face of a cone, πrl, is given as a fact, like the cone's volume in the last lesson. The slant length is the long side of the right-angled triangle inside the cone, so Pythagoras (Year 8) finds it when it isn't given. Students often use the height instead of the slant length; ask which one is along the sloping side. All sizes are made up. The silo's base sits on the ground and is not painted; a real silo has a base too, but nobody paints it. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check. Those who chose 116 counted the join; 104 counted the ground." - "Run: hold up a paper cone and cut it open along the slant to show the fan; the arc length is the circumference of the base." - "Paper: the pipe in Investigate and the silo in Make are worked on paper first. Look for faces chosen before any calculating." stuck: - see: A student gets 116.2 m² for the silo. ask: Where the cone sits on the cylinder, can a painter reach that circle? fix: No. Both joined circles are hidden. Paint the wall and the roof only. - see: A student uses 1.5 (the height) in πrl for the roof. ask: Is the height the distance along the sloping side? fix: "No. l is along the slope: 2.5 m." - see: A student gets 6.8 m² for the pipe. ask: Can a painter reach the inside of the hole? fix: "Yes. A hole adds an inside surface: 2 × 3.14 × 0.4 × 2." stretch: "Fill in a square hole through a cube with a cube cap: does the surface area change by the same amount as the volume? What changes if the hole is wider?" support: A printed silo with the five faces labelled and a tick or cross for painted. leads: > Continues AC9M10M01 node 2. Where it leads: Volume of composite objects and the modelling task, then Year 10 measurement error. exit: q: A box stands on top of a bigger box. Why is the surface area of the stack less than the two boxes' surface areas added together? a: The face where they touch is hidden on both, so it counts for neither. explain: > The surface area of a composite object is just the outside faces. Where two solids join, the faces that touch are hidden, so they are left out. A hole through a solid takes away two faces but adds an inside wall, so the surface area can go up. ```

# Mei's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: mei
Mei paints the silo: a wall 6 m tall with a radius of 2 m, and a cone roof with a slant length of 2.5 m.
Curved wall: 2 × 3.14 × 2 × 6 = 75.4 m².
Cone roof: 3.14 × 2 × 2.5 = 15.7 m².
The cone and the cylinder join along a circle, so she adds both circles: 2 × 3.14 × 2² = 25.1 m².
Total: 75.4 + 15.7 + 25.1 = 116.2 m².
# endregion
